close_reason: Fixed in 13d3253: Unknown is now a struct variant {type_name, payload} with hand-rolled (de)serialise pair. Wire round-trip preserved; 5 new tests assert tag and payload fidelity, empty-payload round-trip, known-variant byte-equivalence, missing-@type error, non-string-@type error.
description:
SECTION: Contract underspecification

CONTRACT RISK
EphemeralMessage::Unknown is defined as a UNIT variant with
#[serde(other)] on a #[serde(tag = "@type")] enum
(crate-jmap-chat-types/src/ephemeral.rs:107-125):

  #[serde(tag = "@type")]
  pub enum EphemeralMessage {
      #[serde(rename = "ChatStreamEnable")]  Enable(ChatStreamEnable),
      ...
      #[serde(other)]
      Unknown,
  }

The doc above this enum claims:
  "Unknown @type values deserialize to EphemeralMessage::Unknown
   rather than producing an error, allowing forward-compatible clients."

The "forward-compatible" claim does not hold in the round-trip
direction. Receiving a future-draft frame like

  {"@type":"ChatVideoCallStart","callId":"v1","ringingAt":"..."}

deserialises into EphemeralMessage::Unknown — at which point both
(a) the original @type discriminant string "ChatVideoCallStart" AND
(b) the entire payload (callId, ringingAt, ...) are DISCARDED.

Serialising the resulting EphemeralMessage::Unknown emits
  {"@type":"Unknown"}
because serde resolves the tag from the variant name and there are no
fields to flatten. #[serde(other)] is documented as
deserialise-only — it does not preserve the original tag for
serialise.

WHAT BREAKS FOR CALLERS
Any caller that treats an EphemeralMessage as data to forward,
restream, log, or replay (federation relays, multi-tab session
bridges, push-to-websocket bridges, the workspace's own jmap-testjig)
will silently mangle every frame it doesn't recognize at the current
build. The recipient on the other side sees {"@type":"Unknown"} and
has no way to tell what the original wire message was.

In a federation context (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00),
silent corruption of forwarded WSS frames is a correctness
regression masquerading as forward-compatibility.

The mode-prompt finding JMAP-ly0n.2 noted that the README documents
Unknown as a struct variant while the code defines it as a unit
variant — that finding is about docs/code mismatch. THIS finding is
about the round-trip data loss that the unit-variant shape causes,
independent of the docs/code mismatch. Fixing JMAP-ly0n.2 by aligning
the README to the current unit variant does NOT fix this; it
documents the loss.

RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION
Switch Unknown to a payload-carrying struct variant that captures
both the original tag and the original body:

  #[serde(untagged)]
  Unknown(serde_json::Value)

or

  Unknown { #[serde(rename = "@type")] type_tag: String,
            #[serde(flatten)] payload: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> }

The latter integrates better with the enum's existing #[serde(tag =
"@type")] discipline but requires choosing a serde idiom that
preserves the original tag verbatim on serialise. A round-trip test
for an unknown @type value belongs alongside the existing
stream_disable_roundtrip test.

ORACLE
serde-derive documentation for #[serde(other)] (deserialise-only);
draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00 (federation relays MUST forward
unrecognised frames without modification).
title: EphemeralMessage::Unknown round-trip discards original @type and payload
